beliefs.practice: Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and never hard-code it or commit it to source control; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
Always connect using TLS/SSL (mongodb+srv or tls=true in the URI) and verify server certificates; do not disable certificate validation in production.

Use least-privilege credentials for the app (a database user that only has read/write on sample_fintech_11 and not admin privileges); store credentials in a secret store (Azure Key Vault or environment variables) and rotate them periodically.

Configure the driver's connection pool options (e.g., maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, maxIdleTimeMS) and server selection/connect timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS) rather than using defaults, to avoid resource exhaustion and long hangs during cluster outages.

Enable retryable writes and implement application-level retries with exponential backoff for transient network or rate-limited errors; make write operations idempotent when possible (e.g., upsert with a unique client-generated id).
When inserting many scored articles, use bulkWrite (unordered) or batching rather than one-by-one inserts to improve throughput and reduce round-trips.

Create indexes idempotently at startup using createIndex/createIndexes for the query patterns you expect (e.g., index on tickers array field, published_at timestamp, sentiment_score, and any fields used in sort), and ensure index creation is non-blocking/background where supported.

Add a compound index tailored to the alert query pattern (e.g., { tickers: 1, published_at: -1 } or { tickers: 1, sentiment_score: -1 }) to support efficient lookups for watchlist matching and recent items.
Add a TTL index for ephemeral data (e.g., keep only N days of raw headlines) using expireAfterSeconds on a date field to cap storage costs and simplify housekeeping.

Model documents to support the app's queries: store headline text, extracted tickers as an array, sentiment score and label, model/source metadata, insertion timestamp (ISODate), and any embedding vectors in a dedicated field with predictable shape (e.g., embedding: [float,...]).

Avoid very large documents and large arrays (keep documents well under 16 MB MongoDB limit) and store long article bodies or attachments externally (blob storage) with a link in the document if needed.

If using vector search/embeddings: store embeddings as numeric arrays and create the appropriate vector index type (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) supported by the cluster; keep vector dimensions consistent and index only the fields you plan to search.

Always run explain() on representative queries during development to confirm queries use the intended index and don't trigger COLLSCAN; adjust indexes if explain shows collection scans or high examinedDocuments.
Project only the fields you need in query results (use projection) to minimize network transfer; use server-side filtering and aggregation where possible to reduce app-side processing.

Use server-side upserts for idempotent writes (updateOne with upsert: true) and include a unique business key (e.g., article_id or hash of headline+source) to allow safe retries and avoid duplicate documents.

Protect any outgoing webhook secret/bearer token: store it in env or Key Vault, rotate it, and validate incoming webhook endpoints (e.g., use short-lived tokens or signed payloads); do not hard-code bearer tokens in code or sample files.
Implement graceful shutdown to close the DB client connection pool (client.close()) so the process exits cleanly and avoids leaked connections in the cluster.
Prefer parameterized queries (avoid building query JSON with untrusted string concatenation) and validate/normalize ticker values to reduce risk of injection or accidental expensive queries.
Monitor and set alerts for RU/s or request units, latency, throttling (429s), and connection pool exhaustion; tune app throughput and use autoscale or increase provisioned throughput when necessary.
When seeding demo/watchlist data at startup, make the seeding idempotent (insert if not exists or use upsert) so repeated restarts don’t create duplicates.

Use explain and the database's query profiler / monitoring tools (or the documentdb MCP server tools) to validate index usage and verify the cost of alert queries that join watchlist membership against incoming headlines.
Prefer storing extracted tickers as a normalized array of uppercase strings and create an index on that array field (array index) to allow simple membership checks (e.g., { tickers: 'AAPL' }).
Limit use of skip for pagination (avoid large offsets); use range-based pagination (e.g., published_at + _id) or keep a last-seen cursor to page efficiently for alerting or UI.

Validate and sanitize any third-party/scraped input before storing it (strip control characters, normalize whitespace, truncate to safe lengths) to avoid storing malformed JSON or unexpected binary data.
